# Get the most recent "Total" observation per country for the map and bar charts
latest_total = (
    hiv_knowledge
    .filter(pl.col('sex') == 'Total')
    .sort('time_period_year', descending=True)
    .group_by('alpha_3_code')
    .first()
    .rename({'obs_value': 'hiv_knowledge_pct', 'time_period_year': 'year'})
)
Code 
# 1. Get the most recent "Total" observation per country for the map

recent_data = (
    hiv_knowledge
    .sort('time_period_year', descending=True)
    .group_by(["country", "alpha_3_code"])
    .agg(
        pl.col("obs_value").mean().alias("avg_hiv_knowledge_pct")
    )
)

# 2. Convert the polars dataframe to pandas so it can merge with the map shapes
recent_data_pd = recent_data.to_pandas()

# 3. Load world geometries from Natural Earth shapefile
world = gpd.read_file("https://public.opendatasoft.com/api/explore/v2.1/catalog/datasets/world-administrative-boundaries/exports/shp")

# 4. Merge with our data using ISO 3-letter codes
map_df = recent_data_pd[['alpha_3_code', 'avg_hiv_knowledge_pct']]
world_merged = world.merge(map_df, left_on="iso3", right_on="alpha_3_code", how="outer")
world = world[world.name != "Antarctica"]

# 4. Build the map with the custom gradient

world_map_red = (
    ggplot(world_merged) # Use world_merged as data source
    + geom_map(aes(fill="avg_hiv_knowledge_pct"), color="black", size=0.1) # Black borders for countries
    + scale_fill_gradient(low="#fee5d9", high="#a50f15", na_value="lightgrey") # Light red to dark red
    + theme_void() # Removes axes and background grids
    + labs(
        title="Youth HIV Knowledge Around the World",
        subtitle="Darker red indicates a higher percentage of comprehensive knowledge",
        fill="Knowledge %"
    )
    + theme(figure_size=(12, 6))
)

world_map_red.save("world_map_red.png", width=12, height=6, dpi=300)
